question: When do leg cramps happen most often during pregnancy?
explanation: Leg cramps happen more as the pregnancy progresses and body weight increases. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h1)

question: Why must nurses carefully check out leg cramps in pregnant patients?

options.A: To stop gestational diabetes from starting
options.B: To avoid doing routine blood tests
options.C: To tell normal discomfort apart from serious problems
options.D: To make sure labor is completely pain-free

explanation: Most cramps are harmless, but some can point to serious issues like blood clots or early labor. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h1)

question: The enlarging uterus contributes to leg cramps primarily by doing what?

options.A: Causing immediate rupture of muscle fibers
options.B: Increasing the production of gastric acid
options.C: Compressing pelvic blood vessels and nerves

explanation: The sheer weight of the growing uterus obstructs optimal blood return and nerve signaling from the lower limbs. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h2)

question: An imbalance in which group of minerals is most directly linked to muscle cramps?

options.B: Vitamin A and other fat-soluble vitamins

explanation: These minerals help muscles contract and relax properly. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h2)

question: What does it mean if a pregnant patient has swelling in only one leg along with a cramp?

options.A: It might be a deep vein thrombosis that needs checking
options.B: It means she is drinking too much water
options.C: It shows the baby is lying in the wrong position
options.D: It is a normal change in the third trimester

explanation: Swelling in just one leg can be a warning sign of a blood clot, not just a normal cramp. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h3)

question: What details must be part of a full nursing assessment of pregnancy cramps?

options.A: Where it hurts, when it happens, how bad it is, and other signs
options.B: The birth weight of her older children
options.C: The color of the delivery room she wants
options.D: The mother's mental health check results

explanation: Knowing the exact details of the pain helps tell normal muscle strain apart from medical problems. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h3)

question: How do normal pregnancy leg cramps usually respond to simple physical actions?

options.A: They go away fast with stretching and massage
options.B: They get worse when you put heat on them
options.C: They need emergency medicine through a vein
options.D: They stay the same for two whole days

explanation: Simple stretching helps stop the sudden muscle tightening of a normal cramp. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h4)

question: Which sign helps tell the difference between early labor contractions and a normal tummy cramp?

options.B: Pain that only happens during hard exercise
options.C: Red skin on the outer thigh
options.D: Feeling better after drinking cold water

explanation: Early labor involves regular womb contractions that often come with pelvic pressure. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h4)

question: A pregnant patient wakes up with a sharp calf cramp. What should she do right away?

options.A: Stand up and walk up stairs fast
options.B: Straighten her leg and pull her toes up toward her shin
options.C: Put an ice pack right on the tight muscle
options.D: Point her toes down hard and massage her kneecap

explanation: Pulling the toes upward stretches the calf muscle and stops the spasm quickly. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h5)

question: Which daily habit helps stop pregnancy leg cramps before they start?

options.A: Wearing high heels to support the calf muscles
options.B: Staying completely still all through the third trimester
options.C: Avoiding standing for too long and not crossing legs at the knee
options.D: Drinking less water to lower pelvic pressure

explanation: Keeping pressure off blood vessels and nerves stops blood from pooling and causing cramps. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h5)

question: Why is drinking plenty of water important for preventing cramps?

options.A: To keep the body hydrated and balance electrolytes
options.B: To build up fat in the legs
options.C: To slow down blood flow and stop the baby from growing
options.D: To flush extra red blood cells out of the kidneys

explanation: Good hydration keeps mineral levels steady and helps muscles work well. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h6)

question: Which foods contain the minerals needed for healthy muscles?

options.D: Green leafy vegetables, nuts, and dairy products

explanation: Foods like greens, nuts, and milk provide the calcium and magnesium muscles need. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h6)

question: What is a good nursing diagnosis for a patient who has painful pregnancy cramps often?
explanation: Muscle cramps cause sudden, sharp pain that fits the nursing diagnosis of acute pain. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h7)

question: What is the main benefit of teaching patients about pregnancy cramps?

options.A: It means the patient never needs to visit the clinic again
options.B: It lowers worry and teaches safe self-care
options.C: It makes sure the baby arrives right on the due date
options.D: It stops all body changes in blood circulation

explanation: Mothers who know what to expect can handle minor discomforts on their own and spot danger signs early. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h7)
